mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within 3 months indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over 3 months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over 3 months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates a slowing economy.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 2% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3% and PAYEMS falls > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where both UNRATE rose by more than 0.3% and PAYEMS fell by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a sharp increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% during a period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2%) signals strong consumer demand, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 2% in 1 month and CPIAUCSL < 2%
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 2% and CPIAUCSL was below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a combination of decreasing industrial production (INDPRO) and increasing consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals stagflation, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases > 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 1% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where both INDPRO decreased by more than 1% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 1% within 3 months.
